plain_english_policy: This bill establishes a new $5 fee for every criminal case (including juvenile, traffic, and quasi-criminal cases) handled by Cleburne County courts. The money collected is split between the Circuit Clerk ($1 per case) and the Sheriff's Office ($4 per case). These funds are specifically designated to support the Calhoun/Cleburne Drug and Violent Crime Task Force for law enforcement expenses, or if that task force dissolves, they remain with the sheriff's department. The fee is only charged when a defendant is found guilty, has their bond forfeited, faces a penalty, or gets an arrest warrant issued; it cannot be waived unless the judge determines the person truly cannot pay.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would create a new revenue stream for Cleburne County law enforcement by imposing mandatory fees on criminal defendants in specific circumstances. The primary policy direction is to fund local drug and violent crime initiatives through user-based charges rather than general taxation, while ensuring the funds are legally restricted to their intended task force operations or departmental expenses.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Lindsey (N & P) advanced this legislation.
evidence_quotes: "a docket fee in the amount of five dollars ($5), hereinafter referred to as a drug and violent crime reduction fee, shall be assessed in each case."

"The fees, when collected, shall be distributed monthly as follows: One dollar ($1) per case to the Cleburne County Office of the Circuit Clerk and four dollars ($4) per case to the Cleburne County Sheriff's Office."

"The drug and violent crime reduction fee disbursed to the sheriff may be expended by the sheriff for any and all expenses incurred by the Calhoun/Cleburne Drug and Violent Crime Task Force law enforcement"
